title: Additive Waves — 3D Terrain
author: Karsten Schmidt (toxi / postspectacular.com)
description: A 2D height-field terrain driven by the sum of multiple wave generators (sine, FBM noise, sawtooth, constant offset) defined in Karsten Schmidt's toxiclibscore wave module. Each generator contributes a sinusoidal or procedural height value z(x, y, t); the final terrain height is the sum (or weighted blend) of all contributions. Rendered as a triangle-mesh surface with optional face-shading from the local normal and a simple horizon gradient sky. The original 2009 demo was Karsten's first showcase of `toxi.math.wave.WaveSampler` for procedural terrain; the algorithm generalizes any layered-function field and shows up across the toxiclibs / thi.ng ecosystem as the canonical 'additive waves' example.
math_essence: For each wave generator i with parameters (amplitude a_i, frequency f_i, phase φ_i, speed s_i), compute w_i(x, y, t) = a_i * sin(2π * (f_i · p + s_i * t) + φ_i) where p is (x, y) for the position dimension. The total height h(x, y, t) = Σ w_i(x, y, t) + Σ (fbm_i(x*s, y*s, t*ts) * amp_i). Triangulated as a regular grid of (N×N) vertices, two triangles per cell. Per-vertex color is a vertical gradient (deep blue at low altitude, white at peaks) modulated by a slope term (|∂h/∂x| + |∂h/∂y|) so steep faces darken. Normals are computed by cross-product of neighbouring cell edges.

parameters.name: extent
parameters.description: World-space side length of the terrain.

parameters.name: noise_amp
parameters.description: Amplitude of the layered Perlin / FBM contribution.

parameters.name: noise_scale
parameters.description: Spatial frequency of the noise layer.

parameters.name: time_speed
parameters.description: Animation speed multiplier for all wave generators.

parameters.name: shade_mode
parameters.description: Render style: gradient-shaded surface, wireframe, or flat color.

source_provenance: toxi.math.wave.WaveSampler + a layered FBM field. Ported from the December 2009 toxiclibs post 'Additive waves' (https://web.archive.org/web/2011/http://toxiclibs.org/2009/12/additive-waves/), the original code-bundle shipped with the toxiclibscore 0011 release. The 2D-to-3D extension is the natural generalization that has since appeared in the thi.ng/wave API and in many oF / Processing terrain demos.
